suggestions.issue: The plain_english directly contradicts the (correct) definition. web-verified via ProSoundWeb ('A Detailed Explanation Of The Aux-Fed Subwoofer Technique') and Fulcrum Acoustic ('The Aux-Fed Subwoofer Technique'): an aux-fed subwoofer is a LIVE-SOUND technique where the subs are driven from a console aux send fed only by selected low-frequency channels (kick, bass, etc.), exactly as the definition states. But the plain_english instead describes a home-theater AV receiver's LFE/sub output doing crossover filtering ('the receiver does the filtering... can line the sub up with the main speakers'). That is home-theater bass management, a different concept, and is wrong for this term.
suggestions.suggestion: Rewrite to match the definition: e.g. 'Instead of letting the subs get the whole mix, the engineer uses a dedicated aux send to route only the low-frequency channels (kick, bass, floor toms, synth bass) to the subs. Because only chosen sources reach the subs, the low end stays tight and uncluttered, and unwanted low-frequency energy from vocals, guitars, and cymbals is kept out of the subs.' Remove all AV-receiver/home-theater framing.

suggestions.issue: web-verified (ProSoundWeb, Fulcrum Acoustic): purpose_function describes home-theater bass management ('Enables integrated bass management with receiver, allows receiver-controlled crossover and phase adjustment'), which is not what an aux-fed subwoofer is. The purpose of aux-fed subs is source-selective LF control at the mixing console in live sound.
suggestions.suggestion: Replace with the live-sound purpose: 'Gives the engineer source-by-source control over what reaches the subwoofers, keeping low-frequency muddiness out of the mains, reducing the number of sources contributing sub energy, and allowing sub level to be managed independently of the main L/R mix.'

suggestions.issue: web-verified (ProSoundWeb, Fulcrum Acoustic): practical_application is entirely home-theater ('Home theater systems typically use aux-fed subwoofers for integrated bass management. Receivers with dedicated sub outputs...'). Aux-fed subwoofing is a live-sound/FOH console technique, not a home-theater/AVR practice; this field is factually wrong.
suggestions.suggestion: Replace with live-sound practice: 'At the console the engineer creates a dedicated aux (often post-fader) as the sub feed, dials only low-frequency channels into that aux, and drives the subs from it; care is needed because the sub aux master stays up when the L/R master is pulled down, so the subs must be muted/managed separately.'

suggestions.issue: web-verified (ProSoundWeb, Fulcrum Acoustic): two of the three scenarios describe home-theater AVR LFE wiring ('Wiring a home-theater sub from the AVR's dedicated LFE/sub output', 'Setting the receiver's crossover and phase'), which is not the aux-fed subwoofer technique. Only the third ('double bass' when fed both aux and full-range) fits.
suggestions.suggestion: Replace the two home-theater scenarios with live-sound ones, e.g. 'At FOH, sending only kick, bass, and floor toms to the sub aux so vocals and guitars stay out of the subs' and 'Remembering to mute the sub aux master when muting the main mix, since pulling the L/R fader does not silence aux-fed subs.'
